meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'уббота'). Common feminine noun meaning 'Saturday' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Скажи всем, что в субботу будет вечеринка.
examples.trans: Tell everyone that on Saturday there will be a party.

examples.text: Скажи всем ребятам, что в субботу вечером будет вечеринка.
examples.trans: Tell all the guys that on Saturday evening there will be a party.

examples.text: Каждую субботу в нашем ресторане бронируют абсолютно все столики.
examples.trans: Every Saturday absolutely all the tables in our restaurant are booked.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, go away', paired with 'уходить'.

meanings.en: to get tired, to be tired
meanings.note: Russian past 'я устал(а)' = English 'I'm tired'

examples.trans: She is very tired after work.

examples.text: Самсон, я устал. Мне сегодня ещё в суд идти!
examples.trans: Samson, I'm tired. I still have to go to court today!

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
